t: This is St Helen's Bishopsgate, an Anglican church tucked away in Great St Helen's, just off Bishopsgate. It is named after Helena, the mother of the Roman emperor Constantine, who is honoured as a saint. The church is also a resting place for notable people. Robert Hooke, the polymath who pioneered microscope observation and helped rebuild London after the Great Fire, is buried here. So is Thomas Gresham, the financier who founded the Royal Exchange. The jurist Alberico Gentili, called the father of international law, lies here too, along with the mathematician Edward Brerewood and the judge Sir Julius Caesar.
